On my way home after a long shift, I’ll stop at a drive‑thru and order way more than I’d ever eat with my family—like several meals’ worth—and I’ll eat it all in the car, quickly, until my stomach actually hurts. Sometimes I sit in a dark corner of the parking lot so no one sees me, because I’m embarrassed by how much I’m putting away. I never eat like that in front of my wife or kids.

At the same time, there are stretches where I feel unusually “switched on” for a few days—more talkative, more ideas, more energy even though I’m sleeping less. I’ll feel really confident, almost wired, but it doesn’t quite tip over into anything extreme. Then it kind of fades, and I’m left feeling sluggish and guilty, especially about those eating episodes. It keeps cycling like that, but I’m not sure what to make of it.
D023-D009_h001.question_a:
I drive the early morning route, so my days start around 4 a.m., and honestly the only thing on my mind lately is food. For about the last six months, at least once or twice a week, I’ll have these episodes in the evenings where I just lose control. I’ll stop on the way home, get a bunch of takeaway and snacks, then when my wife and kids go to bed I sit in the kitchen and eat everything, fast, until my stomach hurts and I feel like I can’t breathe properly from being so full. It’s way more than any normal dinner.  

I do it alone on purpose because I’m ashamed of how much I’m putting away and how I look while I’m doing it. Afterwards I feel disgusted with myself and really low.  

Sometimes I’ll have days where I feel a bit more energetic or talkative than usual, like I’ll clean the house after my shift or feel more upbeat, but it never gets to the point where I’m not sleeping, acting wild, spending loads of money, or getting into trouble at work. I get this rush of ideas—projects around the house, routes I’m going to “optimize” at work—even though no one asked me to. I talk nonstop, interrupt people, get really irritable if anyone slows me down. These spells last several days, sometimes over a week, and then I crash back to my usual or even low mood.

After late shifts I’ll swing by a drive‑through and order enough for two, three people, then sit in the parked bus or my car and eat until I’m painfully stuffed. It’s not just a snack—it’s more like what three people would eat. I eat so much my stomach hurts and I feel painfully stuffed, but I still keep picking at things.

I don’t do it in the dining room. I wait until I’m alone in my room, or when my roommate is at an activity, because I’m ashamed of how much I’m putting away. It’s happening at least once a week, sometimes more.

I do get those “up” days where I feel a bit more energetic or chatty than usual, maybe stay up later talking, but I don’t do crazy spending, I’m not running around the halls, and it never gets to where I’m out of control or in any kind of trouble. I’ll come home, everyone goes to bed, and I’ll end up in the kitchen just… grazing at first. Then suddenly it’s half a pizza, leftover pasta, cookies, whatever I can find, all in maybe an hour. I keep going even when my stomach is tight and I feel almost sick, but I still don’t stop. I do it when my husband’s asleep because I’m mortified by how much I’m eating. If I hear anyone come downstairs, I’ll shove things back in the cupboards and pretend I’m just making tea.

At the same time, I’ll have these stretches where I’m oddly “on.” I need less sleep, I’m talking faster in staff meetings, starting big new projects, feeling like I can fix everything at school. It feels good but also a bit wired, like I’m revved up and can’t fully switch off. Then it kind of tapers and I’m just left tired and ashamed about the food.
D023-D009_h025.question_a:
I’m the principal at the high school, so my days are pretty structured, but my eating feels completely out of control. About once or twice a week—sometimes more—I’ll have these episodes in the evenings, and this has been going on for at least three or four months now.

It usually happens after I get home, once my husband has gone to bed or is in another room. I’ll stand in the kitchen and just keep going: leftovers, cereal, ice cream, anything. It’s way more than anyone would normally eat in that amount of time. I keep eating even after I feel painfully full—like I have to loosen my waistband and lie down—but I still keep picking at food. I always do it alone because I’m mortified by how much I’m eating and how fast. I hide the packaging in the outside trash so my family doesn’t see.

Sometimes I do get short bursts of extra energy—maybe I stay up late reorganizing my office or talking more than usual—but they’re mild and never last more than a day or so. They don’t affect my job or judgment the way I’ve heard real mood episodes can. The eating is what feels truly out of control.
D023-D009_h025.question_b:
I’ve been struggling with these episodes for a little over a year now. It tends to happen in these “up” phases I get every few weeks. I’ll be buzzing with energy, sleeping maybe three or four hours and still showing up at school at 6 a.m., talking a mile a minute, starting new programs on a whim, feeling like I can handle everything at once. My staff will tell me to slow down, but I feel almost invincible in those times.

During those stretches, I’ll come home late, still wired, and just start eating. I can go through half a pizza, a carton of ice cream, bags of chips in maybe an hour, way more than what my family eats for dinner. I keep going until my stomach hurts and I feel physically stuffed. I’m so ashamed of it that I wait until my husband and kids are asleep, or I’ll sit in the car in the driveway and eat there so no one sees. 

After a few days of this, I usually crash into this low, tired state, but the guilt about the eating and how impulsive I get during the “highs” just lingers.
